There are many understandable reasons why you might find it difficult to ask for help when you need it. Psychologists have been interested in this [1] for decades, not least because people's widespread [2] to ask for help has led to some high-profile failures.

Asking for help takes [3]. It involves communicating a need on your part—there's something you can't do. [4], you're broadcasting your own weaknesses, which can be [5]. You might worry about coming across as incompetent. You might have [6] about losing control of whatever it is you're asking for help with. [7] someone starts to help, perhaps they'll take over, or get credit for your earlier efforts. Yet another [8] that you might be worried about is being a nuisance or [9] the person you go to for help.

If you struggle with low self-esteem, you might find it especially difficult to [10] for help because you have the added worry of the other person [11] your request. You might see such refusals as implying something [12] about the status of your relationship with them. To [13] these difficulties, try to remind yourself that everyone needs help sometimes. Nobody knows everything and can do everything all by themselves. And while you might [14] coming across as incompetent, there's actually research that shows that advice-seekers are [15] as more competent, not less.

Perhaps most encouraging of all is a paper from 2022 by researchers at Stanford University, in California, that involved a mix of contrived help-seeking interactions and asking people to [16] times they'd sought help in the past. The findings showed that help-seekers generally underestimate how [17] other people will be to help and how good it'll make the help-giver feel (for most people, having the chance to help someone is highly [18]).

So, bear all this in mind the next time you need to ask for help. [19], take care over who you ask and when you ask them. And if someone can't help right now, avoid taking it personally. They might just be too [20], or they might not feel confident about their ability to help.

passages.title: Section II: Reading Comprehension Part A - Text 1
passages.content:
U.S. customers historically tipped people they assumed were earning most of their income via tips, such as restaurant servers earning less than the minimum wage. In the early 2010s, a wide range of businesses started processing purchases with iPads and other digital payment systems. These systems often prompted customers to tip for services that were not previously tipped.

Today's tip requests are often not connected to the salary and service norms that used to determine when and how people tip. Customers in the past nearly always paid tips after receiving a service, such as at the conclusion of a restaurant meal, after getting a haircut or once a pizza was delivered. That timing could reward high-quality service and give workers an incentive to provide it.

It's becoming more common for tips to be requested beforehand. And new tipping technology may even automatically add tips.

The prevalence of digital payment devices has made it easier to ask customers for a tip. That helps explain why tip requests are creeping into new kinds of services. Customers now routinely see menus of suggested default options—often well above 20% of what they owe. The amounts have risen from 10% or less in the 1950s to 15% around the year 2000 to 20% or higher today. This increase is sometimes called tipflation—the expectation of ever-higher tip amounts.

Tipping has always been a vital source of income for workers in historically tipped services, like restaurants, where the tipped minimum wage can be as low as US$2.13 an hour. Tip creep and tipflation are now further supplementing the income of many low-wage service workers.

Notably, tipping primarily benefits some of these workers, such as waiters, but not others, such as cooks and dishwashers. To ensure that all employees were paid fair wages, some restaurants banned tipping and increased prices, but this movement toward no-tipping services has largely fizzled out.

So, to increase employee wages without raising prices, more employers are succumbing to the temptations of tip creep and tipflation. However, many customers are frustrated because they feel they are being asked for too high of a tip, too often. And, as our research emphasizes, tipping now seems to be more coercive, less generous and often completely disassociated from service quality.

passages.title: Section II: Reading Comprehension Part A - Text 2
passages.content:
When it was established, the National Health Service (NHS) was visionary: offering high-quality, timely care to meet the dominant needs of the population it served. Nearly 75 years on, with the UK facing very different health challenges, it is clear that the model is out of date.

From life expectancy to cancer and infant mortality rates, we are lagging behind many of our peers. With more than 6.8 million on waitlists, healthcare is becoming increasingly inaccessible for those who cannot opt to pay for private treatment; and the cost of providing healthcare is increasingly squeezing out investment in other public services. As demand for healthcare continues to grow, pressures on the workforce—which is already near breaking point—will only become more acute.

Many of the answers to the crisis in health and care are well rehearsed. We need to be much better at reducing and diverting demand on health services, rather than simply managing it. Much more needs to be invested in communities and primary care to reduce our reliance on hospitals. And capacity in social care needs to be greater, to support the growing number of people living with long-term conditions.

Yet despite two decades of strategies and a number of major health reforms, we have failed to make meaningful progress on any of these aims. That is why the Reform think tank is launching a new programme of work entitled "Reimagining health", supported by ten former health ministers. Together, we are calling for a much more open and honest conversation about the future of health in the UK, and an "urgent rethink" of the hospital-centric model we retain.

This must begin with the question of how we maximise the health of the nation, rather than "fix" the NHS. It is estimated, for example, that healthcare accounts for only about 20% of health outcomes. Much more important are the places we live, work and socialise—yet there is no clear cross-government strategy for improving these social determinants of health. Worse, when policies like the national obesity strategy are scrapped, taxpayers are left with the heavy price tag of treating the illnesses, like diabetes, that result.

Reform wants to ask how power and resources should be distributed in our health system. What health functions should remain at the centre, and what should be given to local leaders, often responsible for services that create health, and with a much better understanding of the needs of their populations?

passages.title: Section II: Reading Comprehension Part A - Text 3
passages.content:
Heat action plans, or HAPs, have been proliferating in India in the past few years. In general, an HAP spells out when and how officials should issue heat warnings and alert hospitals and other institutions. Nagpur's plan, for instance, calls for hospitals to set aside "cold wards" in the summer for treating heatstroke patients, and advises builders to give construction laborers a break from work on very hot days.

But implementation of existing HAPs has been uneven, according to a report from the Center for Policy Research. Many lack adequate funding, it found. And their triggering thresholds often are not customized to the local climate. In some areas, high daytime temperatures alone might serve as an adequate trigger for alerts. But in other places, nighttime temperatures or humidity might be as important a gauge of risk as daytime highs.

Mumbai's April heatstroke deaths highlighted the need for more nuanced and localized warnings, researchers say. That day's high temperature of roughly 36°C was 1°C shy of the heat wave alert threshold for coastal cities set by national meteorological authorities. But the effects of the heat were amplified by humidity—an often neglected factor in heat alert systems—and the lack of shade at the late-morning outdoor ceremony.

To help improve HAPs, urban planner Kotharkar's team is working on a model plan that outlines best practices and could be adapted to local conditions. Among other things, she says, all cities should create a vulnerability map to help focus responses on the populations most at risk.

Such mapping doesn't need to be complex, Kotharkar says. "A useful map can be created by looking at even a few key parameters." For example, neighborhoods with a large elderly population or informal dwellings that cope poorly with heat could get special warnings or be bolstered with cooling centers. The Nagpur project has already created a risk and vulnerability map, which enabled Kotharkar to tell officials which neighborhoods to focus on in the event of a heat wave this summer.

HAPs shouldn't just include short-term emergency responses, researchers say, but also recommend medium-to-long-term measures that could make communities cooler. In Nagpur, for example, Kotharkar's team has been able to advise city officials about where to plant trees to provide shade. HAPs could also guide efforts to retrofit homes or modify building regulations. "Reducing deaths in an emergency is good target to have, but it's the lowest target," says climate researcher Chandni Singh.

passages.title: Section II: Reading Comprehension Part A - Text 4
passages.content:
Navigating beyond the organised pavements and parks of our urban spaces, desire paths are the unofficial footprints of a community, revealing the unspoken preferences, shared shortcuts and collective choices of humans. Often appearing as trodden dirt tracks through otherwise neat green spaces, these routes of collective disobedience cut corners, bisect lawns and cross hills, representing the natural capability of people (and animals) to go from point A to point B most effectively.

Urban planners interpret desire paths as more than just convenient shortcuts; they offer valuable insights into the dynamics between planning and behaviour. Ohio State University allowed its students to navigate the Oval, a lawn in the centre of campus, freely, then proceeded to pave the desire paths, creating a web of effective routes students had established.

Yet, reluctance persists among other planners to integrate desire paths into formal plans, citing concerns about safety, environmental impact, or primarily, aesthetics. A Reddit webpage devoted to the phenomenon, boasting nearly 50,000 members, showcases images of local desire paths adorned with signs instructing pedestrians to adhere to designated walkways, underscoring the rebellious nature inherent in these human-made tracks. This clash highlights an ongoing struggle between the organic, user-driven evolution of public spaces and the desire for a visually curated and controlled urban environment.

The Wickquasgeck Trail is an example of a historical desire path, created by Native Americans to cross the forests of Manhattan and move between settlements quickly. This trail, when Dutch colonists arrived, was widened and made into one of the main trade roads across the island, known at the time as de Heere Straat, or Gentlemen's Street. Following the British assumption of control in New York, the street was renamed Broadway. Notably, Broadway stands out as one of the few areas in NYC that defies the grid-based system applied to the rest of the city, cutting a diagonal across parts of the city.

In online spaces, desire paths have sparked a fascination that can approach obsession, with the Reddit page serving as a hub. Contributors offer a wide array of stories, from little-known new shortcuts to long-established alternate routes.

Animal desire paths, such as ducks forging trails through frozen ponds or dogs carving direct routes in gardens, highlight the adaptability of these trails in both human and animal experiences. As desire paths criss-cross through both physical and virtual landscapes, they stand as a proof of the collective insistence on forging unconventional routes and embracing the spirit of communal choice.

passages.title: Section II: Reading Comprehension Part B
passages.content:
Five Steps to Suggesting a Change at Work That'll Actually Get Taken Seriously

[A] Stay positive
[B] Respect the past
[C] Use channels
[D] Give it time
[E] Invite resistance
[F] Be a salesman
[G] Be humble

Everyone wants to be that person—the one who looks at the same information as everyone else, but who sees a fresh, innovative solution. However, it takes more than simply having a good idea. How you share it is as important as the suggestion itself. Why? Because writing a new script—literally or figuratively—means that other team members will have to adapt to something new. So whether you're suggesting a (seemingly) benign change like streamlining outdated protocol, or a bigger change like adding an hour to each workday so people can leave early on Fridays, you're asking others to reimagine their workflow or schedule. Not to mention, if the process you're scrapping is one someone else suggested, there's the possibility of hurt feelings. To gain buy-in on an innovative, new idea, follow these steps:

[41] Great ideas don't stand alone. In other words, you can't mention your suggestion once and expect it to be adopted. To see a change, you'll need to champion your plan and sell its merits. In addition, you need to be willing to stand up to scrutiny and criticism and be prepared to explain your innovation in different ways for various audiences.

[42] Sometimes it makes sense to go to your boss first. But other times, it's useful to build a coalition among your co-workers or other stakeholders. When it works, it works great—because you're ready for your stubborn supervisor's pushback with answers like, "Actually, I connected with a few people in our tech department to discuss how much time these kinds of website updates would take, and they suggested they have the bandwidth."

[43] One of the biggest barriers to gaining buy-in occurs when the owner of an idea is viewed as argumentative, defensive, or close-minded. Because, let's be honest: No one likes a know-it-all. So, if people disagree with you, don't be indignant. Instead, listen to their concerns fully, try to understand their perspective, and include their concerns (and possible remedies) in future discussions. So, instead of saying, "Martha, our current slogan is confusing and should be updated," you could try, "Martha raises a great point that our current slogan has a long history for our stakeholders, but I wonder if we might be able to brainstorm a tagline that could build on that—and be clearer for new customers."

[44] New ideas are the grandchildren of old ones. In other words, don't throw old solutions under the bus to make your improvement stand out. Remember that in light of whatever the problem the old system solved—or, maybe, has failed to solve in recent memory—it was a great idea at the time. Appreciating the older contributions as you suggest future innovations helps bolster the credibility of your idea.

[45] When pitching a new idea, it's important to use the language of abundance instead of the language of deficit. Instead of saying what is wrong, broken, or suboptimal, talk about what is right, fixable, or ideal. For example, try, "I can see lots of applications for this new approach" rather than, "This innovation is the only way." Be optimistic but realistic, and you will stand out.

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [1] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］上下文指代与名词词义辨析。
［解题思路］首句指出“当你需要帮助时，有许多情有可原的理由会令你觉得难以开口”；空格句以 this [1] 回指上文所述心理现象，说明“心理学家几十年来一直对这个[1]（问题、议题）很感兴趣”。question 在此指供探讨研究的社会心理“课题/问题”，与句首“为何难求助”呼应，故选［D］。
［错项排除］［A］illusion（错觉、幻觉）指虚幻不实的错认，而“难以开口求助”是客观普遍心理事实；［B］discussion（讨论）指讨论行为本身，与句中 interested in this... 搭配不够自然；［C］tradition（传统、惯例）偏离科学研究对象语境。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [2] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］句内因果逻辑与上下文态度照应。
［解题思路］逗号前后存在明确的“原因→结果”关联：“尤其因为人们普遍[2]求助（people's widespread [2] to ask for help）导致了一些备受瞩目的失败案例”。结合全文主题“不愿或不敢开口求助”，reluctance（不情愿、抗拒、勉强）与前句 difficult to ask for help 及负面失败后果严丝合缝，故选［A］。
［错项排除］［B］ambition（志向、野心）属积极进取愿望，不合求助心理阻力及“导致失败”语境；［C］tendency（倾向、趋势）中性偏平，缺乏抗拒阻力色彩（且通常倾向于正面或习惯动作）；［D］enthusiasm（热情）则与文意完全相反。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [3] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］上下文语义与段落核心观点。
［解题思路］本段围绕“求助面临重重心理顾虑”展开，紧接句指出“求助需要承认自己做不到、暴露弱点并承担控制权丧失等风险”。可见提出求助本身需要跨越心理关口，需要“[3]（勇气、胆量）”，故选［C］courage。
［错项排除］［A］attention（注意力）关注细节而非克服心理怯懦；［B］talent（天赋、才能）暗示求助需依赖天生禀赋，与下文剖析众人共有的心理障碍无关；［D］patience（耐心）偏重等待耐久力，不能呼应克服怯懦胆怯之意。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [4] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］句间同义释义逻辑与短语辨析。
［解题思路］前句指出“求助需要表达自己的需要，也就是有些事情你做不到（there is something you can't do）”；紧接空格句从本质上重新解读这一行为：“你是在向外界宣扬自己的弱点（broadcasting your own weaknesses）”。两句语义等价、表层与深层互相诠释，故需填入表“换言之、也就是说”的［B］In other words。
［错项排除］［A］At any time（随时随地）抹杀了“仅在开口求助特定情形下”的条件限制；［C］By all means（无论如何、务必）与［D］On the contrary（恰恰相反）分别表示强烈允许或直接语义对立，均不符合前后同义换言逻辑。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [5] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］句内情感语境与形容词辨析。
［解题思路］非限制性定语从句中的 which 指代前文“将自己的弱点公之于众（broadcasting your own weaknesses）”，这自然是一种令人“[5]（不自在的、局促不安的）”体验（can be [5]）。uncomfortable 精准刻画暴露短板时的尴尬抵触情绪，与下文一连串忧虑并列，故选［D］。
［错项排除］［A］unrealistic（不切实际的）多修饰想法或计划，不修饰正在经历的心理体验；［B］deceptive（欺骗性的）暗示假装不能以博取同情，偏离真诚求助困境；［C］tiresome（令人厌烦的、繁琐的）侧重枯燥耗神，未能抓住尴尬不安的痛点。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [6] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］上下文语义与名词搭配辨析。
［解题思路］句内指出：“无论你寻求帮助的是什么事，你都可能对失去对它的控制权存在[6]（顾虑、担忧）。”紧接下句“一旦别人介入，也许会接管并抢功”正是对这种忧虑的解释，have concerns about 为表达“对……心存顾虑”的地道固定搭配，故选［B］。
［错项排除］［A］doubts（怀疑）带入后表示“你怀疑自己会失去控制权”（意即不相信会失控），与下句直接担心他人抢功接管相矛盾；［C］suggestions（建议）与［D］secrets（秘密）皆无法接 about losing control 表心理顾忌。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [7] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］句内条件逻辑与连词辨析。
［解题思路］本句细化“怕失控”的具体担忧：“[7]有人开始帮忙，说不定他们就会接手甚至把你的辛勤功劳占为己有。”这里以一般现在时引导假设触发条件，主句指出由此引发的担忧结果，Once（一旦……就）精准连接假设与后果，故选［A］。
［错项排除］［B］Unless（除非）导致主从逻辑反向悖谬（变成“除非没人帮忙，否则就会抢功”）；［C］Although（尽管）表示让步转折；［D］Before（在……之前）表示“在对方还没帮忙前就已经接管”，不合时序与事理。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [8] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］上下文并列脉络与名词辨析。
［解题思路］句首 Yet another [8] 承接上段已剖析的“怕暴露弱点”“怕失控被抢功”两点心理阻力，进一步引出求助者还可能担心的另一个重要“[8]（因素、层面）”，即害怕成为别人负担（being a nuisance）。factor（因素、要素）恰当地并列归纳各项阻因，故选［C］。
［错项排除］［A］theory（理论、未证实猜想）过高估了普通求助者的顾虑属性；［B］choice（选择）与下文畏惧被动成为累赘冲突；［D］context（语境、背景）通常不用于被担忧的心理障碍本身（be worried about context 不自然）。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [9] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］句内并列语义与动名词搭配。
［解题思路］句尾由 or 连接两个并列表语“给求助对象[9]或者成为一个累赘（being a nuisance）”。因此空格动词短语必须表达给他人带来的“打扰、烦扰或不便”，inconveniencing（给……添麻烦）与“变成累赘”语义完全同向呼应，故选［D］。
［错项排除］［A］overpraising（过分奉承夸赞）虽可能伴随求助，但属个人可控行为而非惧怕沦为负担的消极后果；［B］outperforming（胜过、表现优于）与求助语境反向；［C］reassessing（重新评估）与“成为麻烦”无关。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [10] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］上下文语义与固定动词短语。
［解题思路］句内指出：“如果你深受自卑感困扰，你可能会觉得特别难以[10]寻求帮助（[10] for help）。”reach out for sth 意为“主动伸出援手获取/向他人主动寻求（帮助）”，既地道又精准呼应开篇 ask for help，故选［A］。
［错项排除］［B］settle down（安定下来、静下心）；［C］turn over（翻转、移交）；［D］look back（回顾、回头看），三者均不与 for help 构成“主动向人求助”的动介搭配。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [11] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］上下文同义复现与动词熟词僻义。
［解题思路］紧随空格后的次句出现关键词 such refusals（这样的拒绝），由此即可倒推出空格部分“你还额外担心对方会[11]你的请求”指的必是“回绝、婉拒”。decline 的熟词僻义即为“谢绝、婉拒（请求/邀请）”，与下句 refusals 构成原义复现，故选［A］declining。
［错项排除］［B］considering（考虑）、［C］criticizing（批评）及［D］evaluating（评估）虽各有动作语义，但均不能直接对应下句的 such refusals（拒绝）。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [12] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］句内语境与情感形容词辨析。
［解题思路］高自卑敏感者最怕请求被拒，因为他们容易把对方拒绝看作是在暗示双方人际关系中出现了某些“[12]（负面的、糟糕的）”苗头（something [12] about the status of your relationship）。negative 准确传递“对关系状况作出悲观负面解读”的忧惧心理，故选［B］。
［错项排除］［A］unnecessary（不必要的）通常评价措施或物品，不用于形容担忧关系出了负向裂痕；［C］strange（奇怪的）语义模糊且缺乏自卑者害怕关系恶化的痛感；［D］impractical（不切实际的）不修饰人际关系状态。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [13] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］段际脉络转折与动词搭配。
［解题思路］第三段正式从前两段的“求助为何难”过渡至“如何破局打消顾虑”。首句以目的状语开篇：“为了[13]（克服、战胜）这些困难（To [13] these difficulties），请试着提醒自己每个人都需要帮助。”overcome difficulties 为高频搭配，且顺理成章引出破解方法，故选［D］。
［错项排除］［A］explain（解释）属于前两段已完成的内容而非本段启下的破局策略；［B］identify（识别）同样已在上文列举完毕；［C］predict（预测）偏离解决当下阻碍的祈使句方向。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [14] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］句内让步逻辑与动词辨析。
［解题思路］句内由 while 引导让步状语从句，呈现“主观担忧”与“客观研究结论”的鲜明反转：“尽管你也许[14]（害怕、担心）给别人留下无能的印象（while you might [14] coming across as incompetent），但研究表明求助者其实会被看作更有能力而非相反。”fear 呼应全文“求助顾虑”基调，故选［D］。
［错项排除］［A］deny（否认）暗示求助者并不觉得自己无能，抹平了句内转折反差；［B］forget（忘记）与［C］miss（错过）均无法衔接“害怕显得无能”与后文打消顾虑的反转逻辑。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [15] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］句内对比逻辑与动词被动搭配。
［解题思路］接续前句“你担心在他人眼里显得（coming across as）无能”，研究反驳指出：事实上求助者会被他人“[15]（看待、视为）更有能力（are [15] as more competent, not less）”。perceive... as... 意为“把……视作/看作……”，精准回击主观臆测，故选［B］perceived。
［错项排除］［A］disguised（伪装成）反指求助者其实无能、只是被包装成有能；［C］followed（跟随）与［D］introduced（介绍）皆不能构成 be ~ed as 表达主观认知评价之义。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [16] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］学术研究设计与动词语义辨析。
［解题思路］斯坦福大学 2022 年发表的论文采用了双轨研究方式：既包含实验设计的求助互动（manufactured help-seeking interactions），也包括让受试者“[16]（回忆、回溯）”自己过往真实的求助经历（[16] past experiences）。recall（回忆）与前项“人工模拟实验”形成“回忆真实过往 vs 现场模拟交互”的经典研究对照，故选［A］。
［错项排除］［B］classify（分类）、［C］analyse（分析）及［D］compare（比较）多为研究人员自身处理数据的方法，而非要求普通受试者报告个人经历的常见诱导步骤。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [17] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］句内并列阳性情感与形容词辨析。
［解题思路］研究结果显示：求助者通常会双双低估两件事——既低估别人有多么“[17]（乐意、愿意）提供帮助（how [17] other people will be to help）”，又低估助人能让对方有多开心（how good it makes the helper feel）。be willing to do sth 与助人收获愉悦构成强烈因果呼应，故选［C］。
［错项排除］［A］brave（勇敢的）主体错置，文段说缺乏勇气的是求助者而非施助者；［B］disapproving（不赞成的）与［D］hesitant（犹豫迟疑的）均与下文“对方乐在其中”的乐观研究结论彻底相反。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [18] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］句内解释呼应与形容词词义辨析。
［解题思路］括弧内句子解释前文“让助人者感觉良好（how good it makes the helper feel）”，指出对大多数人而言，有机会帮别人本身是一件“极有成就感、极为有益令人满足的（highly [18]）”事情。rewarding（令人收获满满的、有成就感的）完美解释为何助人令人心情愉悦，故选［C］。
［错项排除］［A］relaxing（轻松惬意的）指不费力的休闲放松，而助人往往需主动付出时间心力；［B］surprising（令人惊讶的）重点在出乎意料，并非正效价收益感；［D］demanding（费力苛求的）强调负担繁重，与“feel good”正相反。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [19] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］句际并行建议与逻辑副词。
［解题思路］末段连续以祈使句给出行动锦囊：首句呼吁下次求助时记住上述鼓舞人心的结论，次句则补充另一条实用提醒：“[19]（此外、同时），要慎选向谁求助以及何时开口。”两句同属收尾实操建议，呈并列补充关系，Also 顺接自然，故选［B］。
［错项排除］［A］Thus（因此）强加因果（记结论并不推导出必须慎选对象时机）；［C］Finally（最后）虽可列举但下文尚有第三条别往心里去；［D］Instead（反而、取而代之）无中生有地否定前句建议。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [20] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］上下文合理解释与形容词辨析。
［解题思路］末两句安慰遭拒的求助者：若有人无法立刻搭手，切莫觉得是针对你个人；因为他们也许只是太过“[20]（忙碌、脱不开身）”，又或者对自身能否帮上忙信心不足。too busy 与后分句并列提供善意客观的解释，故选［C］。
［错项排除］［A］polite（礼貌的）、［B］proud（骄傲自大的）及［D］lazy（懒惰的）要么反而显得是人品问题引发误会（如傲慢或懒惰，恰好会让人觉得被轻慢），要么与“没能立刻帮忙”逻辑矛盾（礼貌更可能尽量搭把手）。

questions.stem: According to Paragraph 1, the practice of tipping in the U.S. ______.

options.text: was regarded as a sign of generosity
options.content: was regarded as a sign of generosity

options.text: was a way of rewarding diligence
options.content: was a way of rewarding diligence

questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］细节事实题（首段历史渊源定位）。
［精准定位］根据题干关键词 Paragraph 1 与 tipping in the U.S. 定位至第一段首句。该句指出，从历史上看，美国顾客习惯向那些“人们假定主要靠小费维生”的从业者支付小费，典型例子便是“基本时薪低于法定最低工资标准的餐馆服务员（such as restaurant servers earning less than the minimum wage）”。由于基本底薪不足，小费对餐厅服务员而言自然是至关重要的基本生计支撑，故［B］was considered essential for waiters 正确。
［错项排除］［A］被视为慷慨的象征、［C］作为奖励勤奋的方式及［D］在大多数行业属自愿之举虽在全文其余语境偶有似是而非表述，但首段第一句对传统美国小费合法性与普遍前提的界定明确落在“弥补低底薪员工主要收入”。

questions.stem: Compared with tips in the past, today's tips ______.

options.text: are less often requested in advance
options.content: are less often requested in advance

options.text: have less to do with service quality
options.content: have less to do with service quality

questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］对比推断题（今昔小费属性对比）。
［精准定位］根据题干比较对象 tips in the past 与 today's tips 定位至第二段及文章末尾总结句。第二段指出过去小费几乎总是在体验完毕后才付，以此“奖赏优质服务（reward high-quality service）”；而末段末句直接点出当今现状的蜕变——小费如今“显得更具强迫性、缺少慷慨感，且常常与服务质量完全脱钩（often completely disassociated from service quality）”。由此可见如今小费与服务优劣的关系大为削弱，故［C］have less to do with service quality 正确。
［错项排除］［A］支付频率大幅降低与第三、四段“小费索要渗透至各行各业”事实相反；［B］更少预先索要与末句前文“预先要求小费（asked for... before receiving service）”相反；［D］占工人收入比例更低缺乏正文对应。

questions.stem: Tip requests are creeping into new kinds of services as a result of ______.
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］因果细节题（新行业索要小费诱因）。
［精准定位］根据题干关键词 creeping into new kinds of services 定位至第四段。该段开篇明晰因果：“数字支付设备的普及让商家向顾客索要小费变得更轻而易举（The prevalence of digital payment devices has made it easier to ask customers for a tip）；这也解释了为什么如今连以往从未收过小费的新型服务也纷纷出现小费请求。”由此可知正是收银支付科技进步催生了这一蔓延现象，故［A］the advancement of technology 正确。
［错项排除］［B］增加收入的愿望只是商家/雇员潜在动因，原文归因句 That helps explain 明确指向前句的数字设备硬件普及；［C］业务多元化及［D］小费膨胀现象出现系本末倒置（tipflation 本身正是第四段描述的现象统称而非深层原因）。

questions.stem: The movement toward no-tipping services was intended to ______.
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］目的意图题（取消小费改革初衷定位）。
［精准定位］根据题干关键词 movement toward no-tipping services 定位至第六段。文章在此揭示餐饮业内部矛盾：高额小费大多落入前台服务员口袋，而后厨厨师和洗碗工却常被排除在外；“为了确保全体员工都能获得公平报酬（To ensure that all employees were paid fair wages），一些餐馆全面禁止小费并相应提高菜品定价”。可见取消小费运动旨在保障员工收入公平，故［D］guarantee income fairness 正确。
［错项排除］［A］刺激消费、［B］丰富收入来源及［C］维持合理价格均偏离第六段核心——实际上该举措甚至需要“提高菜单价格（increased prices）”而非降价保价。

questions.stem: It can be learned from the last paragraph that tipping ______.

options.text: is becoming a burden for customers
options.content: is becoming a burden for customers

options.text: reflects the need to reduce prices
options.content: reflects the need to reduce prices

questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］段落主旨推断题（末段消费者体验定位）。
［精准定位］根据题干关键词 last paragraph 与 tipping 定位至文章最后一段。末段指出，民众并不拒绝给努力服务的侍者合适小费，问题在于当今普遍让人窝火的“小费膨胀（tipflation）”——“许多顾客倍感沮丧，因为他们觉得索要的小费比例过高、频率太勤，甚至在尚未享受任何服务前便遭伸手讨要”，导致给小费显得愈发具有强制压迫感（more coercive）。这清晰反映出小费正日益沦为消费者的心理及财务负担，故［A］is becoming a burden for customers 正确。
［错项排除］［B］有助于激励优质服务恰被末句“与服务质量完全脱钩”反驳；［C］对商业发展至关重要与前段不少餐馆试水去小费引发争议及流失不符；［D］反映降价需要毫无依据。

questions.stem: According to the first two paragraphs, the NHS ______.

options.text: can barely retain its current employees
options.content: can barely retain its current employees

options.text: is rivalled by private medical services
options.content: is rivalled by private medical services

questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］细节理解题（前两段机构困境概括）。
［精准定位］根据题干关键词 first two paragraphs 与 the NHS 定位至第一、二段。第一段指出 NHS 正面临空前严重的困境，第二段以具体数据展开论证：“超过 680 万人仍在排队候诊名单上，医疗服务变得愈发可望而不可及（healthcare is becoming increasingly inaccessible）；无论患者还是员工均苦不堪言”，而且整体健康指标也落后于同等国家。可见 NHS 当下已难以满足民众的正常医疗需求，故［B］can hardly satisfy people's needs 正确。
［错项排除］［A］资金短缺困扰偏颇，首段强调投入经费早已大增（Even with... the budget growing significantly）但表现依旧乏力，即并非单纯差钱；［C］难以留住现有员工在原文两段未曾重点提及（只言 staff suffering 压力大）；［D］受到私营医疗冲击在前两段全无影子。

questions.stem: One answer to the crisis in health and care is to ______.

options.text: lighten the burden on social care
options.content: lighten the burden on social care

questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］细节事实题（医疗危机解决对策定位）。
［精准定位］根据题干关键词 answer to the crisis in health and care 定位至第三段。针对医院人满为患的危机，作者提出切实方向：“要在医院与社区之间重新平衡投入，必须在基层社区和初级保健上投入更多（Much more needs to be invested in communities and primary care），以降低我们对大型医院体系的过度依赖。”选项［C］increase resources for primary care（增加初级医疗保健资源）准确复现核心对策，故正确。
［错项排除］［A］提升大医院内部效率及［B］减轻社会护理负担偏离作者核心提议“分流至初级社区医疗而非继续独木难支堆高大医院投入”；［D］减轻社区压力正好反向——原文主张向社区倾注资源强化社区分担能力。

questions.stem: "Reimagining health" is aimed to ______.
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］主旨目标题（专栏项目意图定位）。
［精准定位］根据题干关键词 Reimagining health 定位至第四段。文中提到智库 Reform 发起该项目，旨在呼吁“对我们延续至今的以医院为核心的模式进行紧迫反思（urgent rethink of the hospital-centric model）”；并围绕一个关键问题展开探索：在医疗卫生体制内部应当如何重新分配权力与资源（how power and resources should be distributed in our health system）。由此可见该项目志在重塑与重构整个医疗体系，故［C］restructure the health system 正确。
［错项排除］［A］强化医院管理仍停留在被批评的“以医院为中心”旧框架内；［B］调整医疗行业法规及［D］重启搁置的医疗改革在第四段均未作为该项目的根本目标出现。

questions.stem: To maximise the nation's health, the author suggests ______.

options.text: paying due attention to social factors
options.content: paying due attention to social factors

options.text: enhancing the quality of health care
options.content: enhancing the quality of health care

questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］细节建议题（国民健康决定因素定位）。
［精准定位］根据题干关键词 maximise the nation's health 与 author suggests 定位至第五段。作者明确指出医疗救治其实只决定了约 20% 的健康结果（healthcare accounts for only about 20% of health outcomes）；“远比医疗本身更为重要的是我们生活、工作、社交的地点以及饮食质量——然而公共政策几乎没有关注改善这些健康的社会决定因素（improving these social determinants of health）”。作者意在呼吁正视并着力改善这些社会影响因子，故［B］paying due attention to social factors 正确。
［错项排除］［A］出台相关税收政策（原文仅批评预算和政策忽视了社会因素）；［C］重新评估主要健康指标与［D］提升医疗服务质量均错把占比仅 20% 的传统医疗环节当作最大抓手。

questions.stem: It can be inferred that local leaders should ______.

options.text: develop a stronger sense of responsibility
options.content: develop a stronger sense of responsibility

options.text: play a bigger role in the health system
options.content: play a bigger role in the health system

questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］推理判断题（末段权力下放诉求定位）。
［精准定位］根据题干关键词 local leaders should 定位至最后一段。末段末尾以设问作结，直言重构系统时必须直面“哪些卫生职能应留在中央，而哪些应该下放给最了解当地民众真实需求的市级、地区及社区领导人（what should be given to local leaders... with a much better understanding of the needs of their populations）”。言下之意正是倡导赋权地方、让地方领导在医疗卫生体系中扮演更重要的角色，故［C］play a bigger role in the health system 正确。
［错项排除］［A］更合理地行使手中现有权力回避了“中央向地方放权”的核心；［B］培养更高责任感偏离体制权责分配；［D］更好了解民众需求其实原文已肯定地方原本就“much better understanding”，关键在于能否获权落实。

questions.stem: According to Paragraph 1, Nagpur's plan proposes measures to ______.
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］细节事实题（首段地方应对措施定位）。
［精准定位］根据题干关键词 Paragraph 1 与 Nagpur's plan 定位至第一段。作为印度高温重镇，那格浦尔市早在 2016 年便出台行动计划：例如要求医院在夏季专为救治中暑病例预留“降温病房（cold wards）”，并建议建筑工地在酷暑日停工休整。不难看出这一系列举措都是为了积极应对高温等极端天气事件，故［A］tackle extreme weather 正确。
［错项排除］［B］保证建筑质量篡改了“工地在酷暑日停工防暑”的主旨；［C］监测紧急警报在第一段尚未触及（属于第二段全印计划争议）；［D］解决超负荷工作量把极端热天临时停工曲解为日常劳工工时改革。

questions.stem: One problem with existing HAPs is that they ______.

options.text: prove too costly to be implemented
options.content: prove too costly to be implemented

options.text: give delayed responses to heat waves
options.content: give delayed responses to heat waves

questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］事实细节题（既有计划短板定位）。
［精准定位］根据题干关键词 problem with existing HAPs 定位至第二段。2023 年一项针对全印 37 份现存高温行动计划的评估报告发现其落实情况参差不齐，直指两大症结之一在于“其触发预警的门槛阈值往往未能结合当地具体气候特征加以量身定制（triggering thresholds often are not customized to the local climate）”，例如沿海高湿地区照搬了干燥内陆的标准。这正说明现行 HAPs 缺乏因地制宜的本地化预警标准，故［B］lack localized alert-issuing criteria 正确。
［错项排除］［A］实施成本过于高昂与原文提及“缺乏足够资金（underfunded）”不是一回事；［C］对热浪响应滞后与［D］令医院承压过重均不是第二段报告指出的触发机制标准漏洞。

questions.stem: Mumbai's case shows that India's heat alert systems need to ______.

options.text: take subtle weather changes into account
options.content: take subtle weather changes into account

options.text: draw further support from local authorities
options.content: draw further support from local authorities

questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］例证目的题（个案折射制度缺陷定位）。
［精准定位］根据题干关键词 Mumbai's case 与 heat alert systems 定位至第三段。2023 年 4 月孟买发生中暑死亡悲剧当天，当地气温约 36℃，甚至还比国家气象局划定的热浪预警线低了 1℃；研究人员复盘指明致命真凶：“高温的危害被高湿度（humidity）——预警系统中常被忽视的一个因子——以及缺乏遮荫处急剧放大”。由此可知高温预警体系不能唯温度论，急需纳入温度以外的其他环境风险要素，故［A］include other factors besides temperature 正确。
［错项排除］［B］把微妙天气变化算入偏离“湿度/遮阳等跨维度指标”；［C］优先关注潜在灾难级热浪忽视了“未达传统温度门槛却因高湿照样夺命”；［D］争取地方政府进一步支持偏离个案揭示的气象技术标准缺失。

questions.stem: Kotharkar holds that a vulnerability map can help ______.

options.text: prevent the harm of high humidity
options.content: prevent the harm of high humidity

options.text: make relief plans for heat-stricken people
options.content: make relief plans for heat-stricken people

questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］人物观点题（科研学者建议工具作用定位）。
［精准定位］根据题干人名 Kotharkar 与关键词 vulnerability map 定位至第四、五段。学者 Kotharkar 在第四段末尾建议绘制脆弱性分布图，以便“帮助将应急响应资源精准集中到风险最高的人群（focus responses on the populations most at risk）”；紧接第五段展开他在那格浦尔的实践成效：那份结合了收入水平、供水管道与遮荫状况的多指标地图“能清晰告知官员究竟应当重点关照哪些街区（tell officials which neighborhoods to focus on）”。选项［B］target areas needing special attention（锁定并瞄准最需要特别关注的区域）贴切概括，故正确。
［错项排除］［A］杜绝高湿伤害（地图主要用于精准筛选高危区域配置资源而非直接改变大气湿度）；［C］扩大那格浦尔项目覆盖面及［D］为中暑者制定具体医疗救治方案皆非脆弱性地图的直接定位功能。

questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］段落推断题（末段未来改进愿景定位）。
［精准定位］根据题干关键词 last paragraph 与 researchers suggest that HAPs should 定位至最后一段。研究人员主张高温行动计划不能仅仅停留在“短期应急抢救（short-term emergency responses）”（如发预警避暑减死），更应纳入“让社区长久凉爽下来的中长期举措（medium-to-long-term measures）”，并且应当“指导房屋节能翻新或修订建筑规范（guide efforts to retrofit homes or modify building regulations）”，涵盖种植城市行道树与防热屋顶绿化等。可见学界呼吁 HAPs 服务于更广泛深远的目标，故［D］serve a broader range of purposes 正确。
［错项排除］［A］把更多精力集中在现症中暑救治恰与呼吁突破短期医疗救急相反；［B］吸引更广泛公众参与及［C］申请更多政府经费虽可能重要，但偏离末段强调功能从短期避险延伸至建筑、城市规划等长远用途。

questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］细节理解题（首段现象定义定位）。
［精准定位］根据题干关键词 Paragraph 1 与 desire paths 定位至第一段。文章定义“欲望路径（desire paths）”为社区留下的非官方足迹、公开秘而不宣的共同偏好与大家踩出来的捷径（shared shortcuts），并进一步解释它们“代表了人类（以及部分动物）沿着阻力最小路径从 A 点最高效抵达 B 点的自然天性（to go from point A to point B most effectively）”。追求高效直达少走弯路正反映了人们图方便的天性倾向，故［C］the tendency to pursue convenience 正确。
［错项排除］［A］探索周围山丘的好奇心、［B］保护绿地的必要性（恰恰相反，踩踏草地往往被认为破坏绿地）以及［D］在独处中寻找慰藉均非首段揭示的捷径动因。

questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］推理判断题（高校案例体现校方态度）。
［精准定位］根据题干关键词 Ohio State University 定位至第二段中间。文章描述俄亥俄州立大学面对学生踩踏椭圆大草坪的行为并未一味设障惩罚，而是“先允许学生自由穿行校园草地，随后顺势将他们踏出的小路直接铺设成正规硬化路面（proceeded to pave the desire paths），从而打造出一张高效实用的通路网”。校方这种顺应尊重学生自然行进需求并予以硬化转正的做法，彰显了校方对欲望路径持肯定积极态度，故［D］takes a positive view of desire paths 正确。
［错项排除］［A］打算改良自身现有欲望路径曲解时态与语义（学校当年并非觉得欲望路径不好要改造它，而是认可并铺平固化学生走出的路线）；［B］引领欲望路径学术研究属无中生有；［C］主动引导规定欲望路径的形成正好与“允许自由走踏（navigate... freely）”之后再顺应铺路相反。

questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］细节理解题（网络图集所折射的社会冲突）。
［精准定位］根据题干关键词 images on the Reddit webpage 定位至第三段。文中提到 Reddit 论坛专题页面收集了无数对比鲜明的照片：人们踏出的斜向泥土捷径旁边，偏偏竖着冷冰冰要求绕行官方铺砖步道的警示牌。作者随后直接点破其深意：“这种冲突凸显了使用者自发需求与追求整齐规划的城市审美愿景之间持续不断的博弈（This clash highlights an ongoing struggle...）”。可见照片反映出关于如何使用与看待欲望路径的分歧对立观点，故［A］conflicting opinions on the use of desire paths 正确。
［错项排除］［B］呼吁全面升级公共空间设计及［C］要求妥善规划欲望路径皆把作者后续反思拔高为图片自带的单一呼吁；［D］对绿地/公共空间丧失的担忧片面夸大了规范派的单方立场，未能反映照片展示的“双方冲突（clash/struggle）”。

questions.stem: The example of the Wickquasgeck Trail illustrates ______.

options.text: the growth of New York City
options.content: the growth of New York City

options.text: the Dutch origin of desire paths
options.content: the Dutch origin of desire paths

questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］例证目的题（历史著名案例作用定位）。
［精准定位］根据题干关键词 Wickquasgeck Trail 定位至第四段。前句指出有些看似草率的捷径最终会突破城市严整的网格规划获得官方的正式认可与永久接纳（permanently recognized）；紧接作者就以美洲原住民在曼哈顿森林穿行踏出的 Wickquasgeck Trail 为例，说明这条泥土小径后来直接演变成为了世界闻名的纽约百老汇大道（Broadway），至今仍斜穿曼哈顿棋盘网格。该知名实例有力论证了民间欲望路径被正式接纳承认的真实历程，故［D］the recognition of desire paths 正确。
［错项排除］［A］说明纽约城市发展扩张与［B］说明欲望路径源自荷兰（原文称荷兰殖民者当年也借用了原住民早就踩出的通道）均系次要背景信息；［C］说明正规城市规划的重要性恰与百老汇打破正交网格格局相悖。

questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］段落推断题（末段人类与动物共性定位）。
［精准定位］根据题干关键词 last paragraph 与 desire paths 定位至最后一段。作者首先拓展视角指出欲望路径并非人类专属（not exclusively human），继而举出鸭子踏穿结冰池塘、家犬在花园抄近道的生动实例（Animal desire paths...），并在首尾呼应指出：这些现象凸显了无论是人类还是动物体验中共通的适应能力与直觉捷径天性（highlight the adaptability of these trails in both human and animal experiences）。这揭示了人与动物在趋利避害、追求阻力最小路径上的共有特征，故［D］show a shared trait in humans and animals 正确。
［错项排除］［A］揭示人类对自然的深切敬畏及［B］对人类心理健康至关重要在末段全无依据；［C］称欲望路径是人类刻意模仿动物行为将并列“共同本能”歪曲成了“模仿借鉴”。

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable subheading from A-G for paragraph [41]:
questions.explanation:
［定位/考点］段落小标题匹配（第[41]段）。
［解题思路］本段开篇点破痛点：“绝妙的点子绝不会孤立自明（Great ideas don't stand alone）”——仅仅提一次建议绝不足以让别人拍板采纳。为此作者要求提案者“积极维护推广自己的方案并大力兜售其优势价值（champion your plan and sell its merits）”，同时做好准备面对挑剔审视，针对不同听众群体的关切以多样化方式反复阐释新想法。像推销员一样主动推广创意、打消受众疑虑正是本段核心，故［F］Be a salesman（做一名推销员）完全契合。
［错项排除］干扰项如［E］Invite resistance 看似与 scrutiny and criticism 沾边，但本段重点在于用多元宣讲主动推销长处并扛住质疑，而非主动邀请反对派提意见（后文第 43 段讲到倾听异议，且那也是保持谦逊）。

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable subheading from A-G for paragraph [42]:
questions.explanation:
［定位/考点］段落小标题匹配（第[42]段）。
［解题思路］本段着重探讨推动变革落地的具体社交与组织路径选择：有时先找直属上司单线沟通顺理成章，而另一些时候则适合先联合平级同事及其他利益相关方结成同盟（build a coalition among your co-workers or other stakeholders）；比如预先私下对接技术部沟通工作量与可行性，再有备无患地应对 stubborn supervisor 的反对。这正是在阐述善于打通上下级及跨部门多方人脉路径来助力提案，故［C］Use channels（善用各方渠道）精准对应。
［错项排除］切勿将［F］的推销优势与本段专门讲求“找准先去找老板还是先找部门同事串联借力”的沟通渠道艺术相混淆。

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable subheading from A-G for paragraph [43]:
questions.explanation:
［定位/考点］段落小标题匹配（第[43]段）。
［解题思路］本段深刻揭示提案推进中最致命的障碍之一：提案人给众人留下“好斗、死不认错、听不进建议、自以为无所不知（argumentative, defensive, or close-minded / No one likes a know-it-all）”的傲慢观感。因此作者告诫千万不要被反对就恼羞成怒（don't be indignant），而是应当充分倾听顾虑、设身处地理解他人的立足点并将各方建议及补救措施纳入后续探讨。与自满傲慢相对的“虚心接纳、收敛锋芒”，正是［G］Be humble（保持谦逊），故正确。
［错项排除］注意区分［G］的“放下‘万事通’身段虚心倾听改进”与下段［B］的“向老一辈历史方案致意”之间的界限；虽同有尊重意味，但本段反讽“know-it-all”直指个人处事须谦卑（humble）。

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable subheading from A-G for paragraph [44]:
questions.explanation:
［定位/考点］段落小标题匹配（第[44]段）。
［解题思路］本段借比喻指出：“新点子都是旧点子的隔代子孙（New ideas are the grandchildren of old ones）”，警示推行创新万不可为了凸显自己方案高明而将过去的旧做法贬得一文不值（don't throw old solutions under the bus）。作者提醒我们：当年旧系统能解决（哪怕近期失效的）特定问题，在彼时也曾是一桩了不起的良策；在提出未来革新的同时珍视前人的既往贡献，不仅有助赢得体谅，还能增强新方案本身的可信度（Appreciating the older contributions as you suggest future innovations helps bolster the credibility of your idea）。由此明显对应［B］Respect the past（尊重过去），故正确。
［错项排除］［D］Give it time 虽偶涉旧制度曾经存续的时间感，但全段旨在表达“对前人成果保持敬意以免树敌”，绝非等待时机。

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable subheading from A-G for paragraph [45]:
questions.explanation:
［定位/考点］段落小标题匹配（第[45]段）。
［解题思路］本段最后谈论游说变革时的语言表达基调：推销新构想时应当多用“充盈积极的词汇（the language of abundance）”，取代挑刺指责的“匮乏负向词句（language of deficit）”；少盯着“哪里出错、破败、次优（wrong, broken, or suboptimal）”做文章，多谈论“什么是可行、可修补或理想状态（right, fixable, or ideal）”，做到乐观而务实（Be optimistic but realistic）。全文紧扣正面积极的心态与措辞，故［A］Stay positive（保持积极乐观）完美收尾，故选 A。
［错项排除］［F］Be a salesman 已分配给专门强调阐释产品优点的第 41 段；本段虽也用 pitching 一词，但其独一无二的重心完全集中在正负用语对比与“optimistic（乐观）”态度上。
